The thorax is the region that occupies the upper part of the trunk, located between the neck at the top and the abdomen at the bottom. Deformable, it participates in respiratory movements. It is surrounded by a musculoskeletal wall. It surrounds and protects the main organs of the circulatory and respiratory systems (heart, lungs, large vessels, etc.).

External configuration Cylindrical in shape in the newborn and slightly flattened conical ventro-dorsally with a lower base in adults. The thorax is made up of a wall and a cavity, it is limited by: At the top by: An upper orifice: located at the base of the neck with which it communicates. At the bottom A lower, wider orifice, closed by a muscular partition: the diaphragm. The latter separates the thoracic cavity from the main abdominal viscera. Dimension: Height: Front: 12 cm, Back: 27cm On the sides: 33 cm Sagittal diameter: At its top: 5 cm - At its base: 12 cm Transverse diameter: At its top: 11 cm - At its base: 26 cm

? posteriorly: the concave side, It gives insertions to several muscles. It has two faces: ventral or anterior, dorsal or posterior And three edges (upper and two lateral which are crenellated). It articulates externally with the ribs via the costal cartilages, above and externally with the clavicles. There are three parts: a- The manubrium:-upper part of the sternum. It is thick, wide, trapezoid-shaped, with a large upper base. It presents: - in its upper and middle part the jugular notch (or sternal fork) - on either side of the jugular notch, the clavicular notches articulate with the clavicles (saddle joints). - laterally and above, the first costal incisure, articular with the first costal cartilage - laterally and below, the half-incisure, intended for the upper half of the second costal cartilage (which straddles the manubrium and the body b- The body of the sternum: narrow and elongated, it has transverse striations corresponding to the lines of fusion of the 6 sternebrae (segmental elements of the sternum). Its lateral edges present successively: - at the top, the half-articular notch with the lower half of the 2nd costal cartilage - the costal notches which receive the costal cartilages of the 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th ribs - at the bottom, a half-notch which receives the upper half of the 7th costal cartilage - Louis angle: located between the manubrium and the body of the sternum, measures on average 15°. lower body. It is cartilaginous, of variable shape (tapered, widened, bifid, etc.) At its upper-lateral ends, there is the half-articular incisure with the lower half of the 7th costal cartilage. II- Ribs The ribs are flat, even and non-symmetrical bones, creating almost the entire rib cage. has 12 pairs of ribs numbered from top to bottom, we distinguish:

? Seven sternal ribs or ?true ribs? which articulate with the sternum: chondro-sternal articulation ? Three ?false ribs? their cartilage unites with that of the seventh rib. ? Two ?floating ribs? (free forward). NB: from the 8th to the 12th ribs are called aternal. 1-Dimension: -The length of the ribs increases from the 1st to the 7th then decreases from the 8th to the last. -The width of the true ribs increases from posterior to anterior, reaching its maximum at the anterior end. - the false ribs are wider at their middle part.

The tubercle: located between the neck and the body of the rib, it has a non-articular part and an articular part with the facet of the transverse process of the corresponding vertebra. c- The ventral end is continued by the costal cartilage - Particularities of the first rib: - smaller than the other ribs, - flattened from top to bottom, it has an upper side and a lower side - does not have a costal groove. - its head has only one articular surface for T1. - Particularities of the 2nd rib: - oblique orientation, intermediate between that of the 1st and 3rd ribs, it does not have a costal groove. - Particularities of the tenth rib: - the head of the tenth rib has a unique facet which articulates with T10. - Particularities of the eleventh and twelfth ribs: - absence of costal tuberosity and neck. - each is articular with the corresponding dorsal vertebra.

III- Thoracic spine The thoracic vertebrae are 12 in number which articulate with the ribs. The thoracic vertebra presents: Vertebral body: cylindrical, with the posterior part of the external face presence of 4 costal dimples, upper and lower. ? Pedicles are rounded and horizontal ? Blades without particularity ? Spinous process: thin, long and inclined downwards ? Transverse processes: oblique outwards and backwards, has a costal articular facet, except for Th11 and Th12 ? Rounded and narrow vertebral foramen IV- Joints of the thorax The costo-vertebral joints namely: * The costo-corporeal joint: It unites the head of a rib to two adjacent vertebral bodies. Type: arthrody *The costo-transverse joint It unites the costal tuberosity to the transverse process of the vertebra of the same number. Type: trochoid *The cervico-vertebral ligaments. Superior cervico-transverse ligament Interosseous costo-transverse ligament Cervico-lamellar ligament The costo-chondral joints: between the rib and the costal cartilage, it is a ? and inter-chondral syndesmosis. of the synovial type, they unite the 6th, 7th, 8th costal cartilages. The chondro-sternal joints. There are seven pairs of joints uniting the sternum to the costal cartilages. With the exception of the 1st and 7th, each of them consists of two arthrodies

V- Thorax muscles

V- Functional anatomy The movements of the rib cage are permanent and accompany breathing. They essentially result from movements of the costovetebral joints. The sterno-costal and interchondral joints are the site of small sliding movements. VI- References
